body.statement: If the rows of \(C\) form an orthonormal basis of the zero-sum contrast space and \(W\) is the identity matrix, then \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\) and \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\neq b\), so \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). Thus common ranks maximize the sum of the randomization variances of a complete orthonormal contrast system, even though Theorem 3 rules out universal Loewner dominance when \(K>2\).
body.justification: This nondegenerate multi-arm case separates a valid omnibus scalarization from invalid joint covariance dominance.
body.gap: Zhao and Ding permit complete contrast systems but do not derive their sharp common-rank covariance-loss endpoint.
body.consumer: Factorial and analysis-of-variance designs obtain an analytic least-favourable total-variance benchmark.
